summary: Standing 80 ft Aermotor tower in Lauderdale County, MS, registered by NHLR in 2022; roof and windows were missing at the visit and the build date is unknown.

facts.design: 80 ft Aermotor tower with a straight internal stair
facts.status_note: Standing, but in rough shape with roof and windows missing at the 2022 register visit

events.note: Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register 10 July 2022; nominated by Jason Johns

evidence.supports: 80 ft Aermotor with a straight internal stair
evidence.quote: 80ft Aermotor with a straight internal stair

evidence.supports: Roof and windows missing; antenna added to the top
evidence.quote: rough shape, missing roof and windows. antenna was added to the top

evidence.supports: Administered by the Mississippi Forestry Commission
Regional index lists it under Mississippi as Meridian
Aermotor towers were made of galvanized steel
evidence.quote: Aermotor towers were made of galvanized steel

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 600 ft (183 m), which matches the brief's 182.9 m. OpenStreetMap gives 190 m. The story uses the register figure.
The register names the Mississippi Forestry Commission as administrator but also says the site was vacated by the commission. Both are reported; no source dates the departure.

sources.title: The Aermotor Company: From Windmills to Forest Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: Thin record: only the NHLR entry, the Forest Lookouts index (name and county only) and the OSM node were usable after two searches. No build date, staffing, fire history, access or visit information found. height_m is converted from the register's 80 ft. No access key set because no source gives access. Unverified lead, not in the story: a localgovs.com listing places the Mississippi Forestry Commission Meridian office at 868 East Fire Tower Road; nothing links it to this tower. Grokipedia and anyplaceamerica appeared in search results and were not used.
